name: Ecommerce Product Page
description: A product page whose gallery and buy box share the first screen: options that say when they're sold out, an Add to cart that is never disabled and points to the missing choice, a sale price read as "was" and "now", and a cart request the server prices.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing components win.

layout.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. The sticky header and the purchase bar are sticky bars; the full-size gallery is a modal.

positioningContract.purchaseRegion: From 1024 px, the gallery and the buy box side by side; on phones, stacked
positioningContract.details: After the purchase region, in the page's flow
positioningContract.purchaseBar: On phones only, fixed at the bottom while the buy box's button is out of the window
positioningContract.fullSizeGallery: A native dialog in the top layer

invariants: The title, the price, the options, Add to cart, and delivery stay together in the buy box
Recommendations come after the decision content
scroll-padding-top and scroll-padding-bottom keep the focused element clear of the sticky header and the purchase bar
Nothing scrolls sideways down to 320 px wide

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Build or extend a product page: the gallery and the buy box in the first screen, options as radio groups, an Add to cart that is never disabled and points to a missing choice, the price in words for screen readers, details, reviews, and recommendations, with a purchase bar on phones. The cart request never sends the price, and a timeout is an unknown outcome. Build on the project's storefront components and commerce platform when it has suitable ones. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: The gallery and the buy box together in the first screen from 1024 px
Thumbnails as named buttons, and a full-size view in a native dialog
Option groups as fieldsets of radios, with sold-out options said in text
An Add to cart that is never disabled: a missing choice gets a message and focus
A cart request without the price, and a timeout treated as an unknown outcome
A purchase bar on phones that submits the same form and never covers the focused element
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, the commerce platform and its product data, and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has product page parts (galleries, option pickers, cart buttons), configure or extend them to meet this guide instead of building others, and keep their APIs.
2. Choose what the task needs: the gallery, options, reviews, the purchase bar, recommendations. Leave out the rest.
3. Lay out the purchase region and the sections after it (layoutModel, components.BuyBox).
4. Build the gallery (components.Gallery) and the price (components.BuyBox.behavior.price).
5. Build the options and the guarded Add to cart (components.BuyBox.behavior.options, frameworkPatterns.guardedAddToCart), and the sending (implementationDetails.sending).
6. Add the purchase bar on phones (components.PurchaseBar), the details, and the reviews (components.Reviews).
7. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, a phone, and 200% zoom, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

Header.description: The store's header, with the skip link and the cart link

Breadcrumbs.description: nav "Breadcrumb": the category path, the product last

PurchaseRegion.description: The gallery and the buy box

Gallery.description: The main image, thumbnails, and the full-size view

BuyBox.description: A form: the h1, the rating, the price, the options, the quantity, Add to cart, delivery and returns

Details.description: Highlights, description, specifications, fit, materials and care, questions

Reviews.description: The summary, the distribution, filters, and the reviews

PurchaseBar.description: Phones only: the price and Add to cart, while the buy box's button is out of the window

StatusRegion.description: One polite status region, present from the start

Gallery.description: The main image, and thumbnails as buttons named after their image ("Front view", "Fabric close-up"), the shown one marked with aria-current="true" and by more than color.

behavior.fullSize: A "View full size" button opens the full-size view in a native <dialog>, as the Modal Dialog guide says: the rest of the page is inert, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the button. Zoom on hover is an extra, never the only way.
behavior.swipe: Swiping between images needs buttons too (WCAG 2.5.1), and works with them alone.
behavior.loading: The first image loads at once with fetchpriority="high"; the others loading="lazy". Every image has width and height, or the gallery an aspect-ratio, so nothing shifts.
behavior.video: A video doesn't play with sound on its own, has visible controls, and has captions when it has speech.

BuyBox.description: The buy box holds, in this order: the product's title (the page's <h1>), the rating summary, the price, the options, the quantity, Add to cart, and delivery and returns. Nothing needed to buy is in a tab or an accordion.

behavior.price: Prices are formatted with Intl.NumberFormat for the currency and the locale, and say whether tax is included where that's required. A compare-at price is struck through, which most screen readers don't announce, so "$58 $48" is unclear. Add visually hidden text: "Was $58, now $48". A saving ("Save 17%") is worked out from the two prices, rounded down.
behavior.options: Each group (color, size) is a <fieldset> with a <legend>, and its options are native radios: one Tab stop, and the arrows choose. The chosen value shows beside the legend ("Size: M"). Color swatches are radios named after the color ("Navy"), drawn as swatches. An option that can't be bought says so in its label ("M, sold out"), not only with a strike-through or a faded color (WCAG 1.4.1). It can be disabled, which the arrows skip (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit); the words in its label are what say why. When a choice in one group makes the chosen option of another unavailable (a size sold out in the new color), that option is cleared, and the status region says so ("M isn't available in Navy"). Price, availability, delivery, and images follow the chosen options. With many options, a select or a combobox (the Select and Combobox guide).
behavior.addToCart: Add to cart is never disabled, since a disabled button can't be focused and doesn't say what's missing. Pressed while an option group has no choice it can send, or while the quantity breaks its rules, it sends nothing, shows each problem's message, and moves focus to the first: the group's first option that can be chosen, or the quantity field. Each message sits in its control's description (aria-describedby on the group's fieldset, or on the field), and is empty while it's hidden, so it adds nothing until it shows; the quantity field also has aria-invalid="true" while its message shows. A message goes as soon as its problem is fixed. Without script, required on the radios and the quantity field's own rules make the browser block the post and focus the first problem (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). The script sets novalidate and shows its own messages instead, as the Form Validation Pattern does, so it checks every rule the browser would have: a check of the option groups alone let quantities 0, 6, 1.5, and an empty one reach the cart (checked in all three). The quantity is a required number field with min="1" and a max that follows the stock, so a fraction fails its step; its message says the range ("Enter a quantity from 1 to 5"). Stepper buttons, if any, are named "Decrease quantity" and "Increase quantity".
behavior.sticky: A sticky buy box on wide screens is optional, and only if it fits the window below the sticky header.

PurchaseBar.description: On phones, a purchase bar with the price and Add to cart appears when the buy box's button has left the window: an IntersectionObserver on that button decides, not a scroll handler. While it's not shown, it's hidden (or inert while it animates), not only moved off screen.

behavior.sameForm: Its button submits the same form with form="…", so the same check runs (checked: the submit event names it as the submitter in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). It's a region named for its purpose, "Quick purchase".
behavior.notObscured: scroll-padding-bottom at its height, with scroll-padding-top at the sticky header's, keeps the focused element clear of both (WCAG 2.2 2.4.11). env(safe-area-inset-bottom) pads it only when the viewport meta tag has viewport-fit=cover.

Details.description: Highlights, the description, specifications (a <dl> or a table with row headers), fit or dimensions, materials and care, and questions. On phones, each can be a <details> with its heading in the <summary>; nothing needed to buy is inside one.

behavior.delivery: Delivery, returns, and pickup sit near Add to cart, in plain text that depends on the shopper's region when it differs.

Reviews.description: A summary near the title: the stars are images, so the rating is text ("4.8 out of 5 stars, 218 reviews"), and it links to the reviews section.

behavior.distributionAndFilters: The distribution's bars have their numbers in text ("5 stars: 70%"). Filtering and sorting say how many reviews show, in the status region, as the Data Table guide's filter does.
behavior.userContent: Review text and answers are user content: rendered as text, never as raw HTML. "Verified purchase" is text, not only an icon.
behavior.empty: With no reviews yet, say so, with a way to write the first.

Recommendations.description: Related products come after the decision content (details and reviews), never before the buy box, shown as the store's usual product cards.

behavior.rail: A horizontal rail scrolls with the keyboard (its links are in the Tab order) and shows that it scrolls, such as a part of the next card; a hidden scrollbar isn't the only cue.

chosenOptions.persistence: The form's radios; optionally mirrored to the URL (?color=navy&size=m)

quantity.description: The quantity field's value, from 1 to the stock.

purchaseBarShown.description: Whether the phone's purchase bar shows.
purchaseBarShown.determination: An IntersectionObserver on the buy box's button, below 1024 px

ssrConsiderations.options: Render the default variant's price and availability, and the options from the URL if it has them, so nothing changes after hydration.
ssrConsiderations.purchaseBar: Render the bar hidden; the observer shows it.

keys.chosenOptions: Optional: the URL's query (?color=navy&size=m), so a link opens the same variant

navigationBehavior.reviewsLink: The rating summary links to the reviews section, which lands below the sticky header through scroll-padding-top.
navigationBehavior.onRouteChange: Close the full-size view, and hide the purchase bar until its observer decides again.

colorContrast.note: See designSystem; check the project's own colors the same way.

designSystem.note: Suggested defaults for projects without a design. The project's tokens and existing components win.
designSystem.sizes: The buy box is 360 to 440 px wide from 1024 px; the title 32 to 44 px (24 to 32 px on phones); the price 28 to 36 px.
designSystem.colors: Text meets 4.5:1, and focus indicators, the chosen option's marker, and form fields' edges 3:1. A message such as "Choose a size" in #b91c1c on white is 6.5:1. Check the project's own colors the same way.
designSystem.targets: Touch targets are at least 44 px, and nothing scrolls sideways at 320 px wide.

implementationDetails.sending: The cart request sends the product, the chosen options, and the quantity, never the price: the server prices the order. While it's out, the button keeps focus with aria-disabled="true" and ignores a second press. The result goes to the page's one polite status region ("Added to your cart: Organic Cotton Tee, M"), the cart's count goes in the cart link's name ("Cart, 2 items"), and a mini cart or a toast is optional. A request that times out may have added the item, so the outcome is unknown, not failed: read the cart again before saying anything, and send a retry with the same request id, so it can't add the item twice. An error that the shopper can fix points to the field it's about, as the missing choice does.
implementationDetails.structuredData: If the project manages structured data, render it on the server from the same data as the page: the product, its offers per option with their own prices and availability, and the rating. Don't hardcode prices into it.
implementationDetails.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. The sticky header and the purchase bar are sticky bars; the full-size gallery is a modal.
implementationDetails.motion: Motion is optional: images cross-fade over 180 ms, and the purchase bar fades in. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, nothing slides.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version.

guardedAddToCart.description: Add to cart is never disabled: with novalidate set, the submit handler checks every rule the browser would have, each option group's choice (a chosen option that became unavailable counts as none) and the quantity's own rules; it shows each problem's message in its control's description, moves focus to the first, and sends nothing, and a message goes as soon as its problem is fixed. The phone's purchase bar submits the same form; without script, the browser checks the same rules.
guardedAddToCart.html: Size

edgeCases.soldOut: Replace Add to cart with a back-in-stock signup, and say "Sold out" in text.
edgeCases.manyOptions: A select or a combobox instead of radios, with the same message and focus on a missing choice.
edgeCases.noReviews: Say so, with a way to write the first.
edgeCases.longTitle: It wraps; the price and Add to cart stay in the first screen on phones.
edgeCases.unknownDelivery: Say so, and ask for a postcode only when the shopper wants the estimate.

must: Build on the project's storefront components and commerce platform when they're suitable, and keep their APIs
Keep the title, the price, the options, Add to cart, and delivery together in the buy box
Send the product, the options, and the quantity to the cart, and let the server price it
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Disable Add to cart to show that a choice is missing
Set novalidate without checking every rule the browser would have checked
Send the price to the cart, or trust a price from the browser
Say an add failed when the request timed out; read the cart again
Show a sold-out option only with a strike-through or a faded color
Put anything needed to buy in a tab or an accordion
Add a dependency, such as a gallery or zoom library, without asking
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: The product's title is the page's h1, and from 1024 px the gallery and the buy box share the first screen
Gallery thumbnails are buttons named after their image, the shown one is marked, and a button opens the full-size view in a native dialog
The first image loads at once with fetchpriority="high", the others lazily, and every image has width and height
Each option group is a fieldset with a legend and radios, and swatches are named after their color
A sold-out option says so in its label, and a choice that makes another one unavailable clears it and says so
A sale price is read as "Was $58, now $48", and prices are formatted for the locale
Add to cart is never disabled: with a missing choice or a quantity outside its rules, it sends nothing, shows each problem's message, and moves focus to the first
Without script, the radios' required and the quantity's required, min, max, and step make the browser block the post the same way
The cart request sends the product, the options, and the quantity, never the price
Adding says the result in the status region; a timeout reads the cart again instead of saying it failed, and a retry can't add the item twice
The phone's purchase bar is hidden until the buy box's button leaves the window, submits the same form, and never covers the focused element
The rating is text ("4.8 out of 5 stars, 218 reviews"), review text is rendered as text, and filtering reviews says how many show
Nothing scrolls sideways at 320 px wide, and touch targets are at least 44 px
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens
